producer_report.summary: Drain now approves open proposals whose rung the raising role may change itself, and works jobs that a work decision records as approved and that are still in state proposed. It leaves above-limit and unknown-role proposals waiting with the "needs a person" text. Closed jobs are not picked up again. The module docs, changelog and roles-and-ladder design doc describe this. This pass made no edits. I re-ran the drain tests and the fmt, clippy and full test checks, and I cite the specific tests as evidence below.

checks_run.note: Ran as `cargo test --locked --quiet` after the plain run's output was too large to read back; all suites ok, 0 failed.

criteria_check.criterion: A drain test gives an open proposal on the implementation rung from a role whose limit covers it. The proposal is approved, its job is read, run and landed, and it is absent from the report's waiting list. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` passes (18 passed, 0 failed). In crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs, `the_real_steps_approve_only_the_in_limit_proposal_and_leave_the_others_waiting` drives RealSteps and asserts: `approvable` is [LOW], one Approved work decision exists for LOW, the lander is asked once for that job, the job is Closed(Landed) with 1 reading, `report.landed == 1`, and `display::drain` text does not contain LOW. `an_in_limit_proposal_is_approved_then_its_job_is_run_and_landed_without_a_second_reading` covers the loop with a stub.

criteria_check.criterion: A drain test shows a proposal above its raising role's limit, or from an unknown role, is neither approved nor worked and still appears as waiting with the "needs a person" text. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
criteria_check.evidence: Same passing run. `the_real_steps_approve_only_the_in_limit_proposal_and_leave_the_others_waiting` seeds an above-limit proposal (HIGH) and an unknown-role proposal (GHOST). It asserts `queue.waiting == [HIGH, GHOST]`, and `steps.approve` on either returns no job and an error. Only one work decision exists, for LOW. `report.waiting == [HIGH, GHOST]` and the rendered text contains "needs a person". `a_proposal_that_needs_a_person_is_listed_waiting_and_left_alone` covers the stub path.

criteria_check.criterion: A drain test shows a job that a work decision records as approved and that is still in state proposed is picked up and run once by drain, and a closed job is not picked up again. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`.
criteria_check.evidence: Same passing run. `an_approved_job_is_picked_up_once_and_a_closed_one_is_not_picked_up_again` approves LOW through `athena.approve_work`, so the job sits in state proposed with 1 reader invocation. `steps.queue()` yields that job with `read == true`. After drain, `landed == 1`, the reader count is still 1, and the lander was called once. A second `queue()` returns no items, and a second drain stops with QueueEmpty and the lander is still called once. `an_approval_that_does_not_fit_the_budget_is_not_made_and_the_proposal_stays_open` and `an_approved_job_still_in_state_proposed_is_run_once_and_not_read_again` cover related paths.

criteria_check.criterion: The module doc in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs no longer contains "has no way to accept, approve or land". It states that in-limit proposals are approved and approved jobs are worked, and that rejecting and approving above-limit proposals stay with people.
criteria_check.evidence: I read drain.rs lines 1-28. The bullet "In-limit proposals are approved, approved jobs are worked" and the bullet "People decide the rest. Rejecting a proposal, and approving one above its role's limit (or from an unknown role), stay with people" are both there. A Grep for "has no way to accept" in drain.rs found no match.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo test` pass for the workspace.
criteria_check.evidence: `cargo fmt --all --check` produced no output. `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` finished clean. `cargo test --locked --quiet` showed every suite as `ok`, with 0 failed (a few ignored tests).

mistakes: My previous report did not give per-criterion evidence for the three drain-test criteria. This report gives it, citing the specific test names and assertions.
learnings: Bash tool output over the size limit is saved outside the working directory, and the policy hook then blocks reading it. Use `cargo test --quiet` to keep output small.
